title: Outlook: folder sharing respects organisation restrictions on Default and Anonymous permissions
summary: Hold: the Cloud Policy instructions omit two policies that Microsoft's procedure requires, and the control's claimed coverage of all Outlook clients is not documented. The risk section also incorrectly implies that the Default entry itself grants every authenticated user access, regardless of its permission level.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls notes; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not identified which restriction this feature reads or documented a feature-specific Default or Anonymous switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Default Anonymous restrictions folder permissions policy; Outlook Default Anonymous folder permissions restrictions default rollout 579185. Read roadmap, folder-restriction article and Cloud Policy overview; no feature-specific mapping or switch found.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not explicitly establish whether classic Outlook or Outlook for Mac is included.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Web"]; description ends with "#newoutlookforwindows".

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a restriction on editing permissions, not a new identity or access path.
claims.quote: When these restrictions are enabled, you won't be able to change either setting. Permissions granted directly to individual users will remain unaffected.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes no agent or automated action.
claims.quote: Folder sharing in Outlook will respect your organization's restrictions for Default and Anonymous permissions. When these restrictions are enabled, you won't be able to change either setting.

claims.claim: The Default entry lets any authenticated user in the organisation reach a folder.
claims.quote: Default applies to authenticated users in the organization who don't have an explicit permission entry. Its typical value is AvailabilityOnly. ... None | No | No | No | No | No calendar access.
claims.fix: Replace with: 'Default determines baseline calendar permissions for authenticated users in the organisation who have no explicit permission entry; the access they receive depends on its assigned permission level.' Do not imply that the entry itself grants folder access.

claims.claim: Increasing Anonymous above None can expose calendar information more broadly than intended.
claims.quote: Increasing Anonymous above None can expose calendar information more broadly than intended.

claims.claim: Policy configurations are found in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center under Customization > Policy Management.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. ... To view a list of policy configurations, select Customization > Policy Management.

claims.claim: The documented Cloud Policy restriction procedure is to enable Do not allow users to change permissions on folders in a policy configuration.
claims.quote: Enable each of the following policies: Turn off sharing recommendation; Do not allow users to change permissions on folders; Control Calendar Sharing.
claims.fix: State the complete documented general procedure in the row note and rendered table: create a policy configuration with the applicable scope, enable 'Turn off sharing recommendation', 'Do not allow users to change permissions on folders', and 'Control Calendar Sharing', then select Update. Retain the caveat that Microsoft has not confirmed this procedure governs roadmap item 579185.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy folder-permission restriction applies to all Outlook clients.
claims.quote: Searched: Do not allow users to change permissions on folders Mac mobile. Read restriction article and Cloud Policy overview; restriction article names classic Outlook, new Outlook and Outlook on the Web, not all clients.
claims.fix: Replace '(all Outlook clients)' with '(classic Outlook, new Outlook and Outlook on the web)' in controls[0].governs and its rendered table row. Do not extend coverage to Mac or mobile without documentation.

claims.claim: No API or automation equivalent is documented for configuring this Cloud Policy folder-permission restriction.
claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy service Microsoft 365 API PowerShell policy configurations Do not allow users to change permissions on folders. Opened folder-restriction article and Cloud Policy overview; no equivalent management API or cmdlet found.

claims.claim: Set DisableEditPermissions and DisableEditDefaultUserPermissions to DWORD value 1 under HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Options\Folders.
claims.quote: Either directly or through Group Policy, set the value of the following registry entries to 1: ... DisableEditPermissions ... DisableEditDefaultUserPermissions ... set their type to DWORD (32-bit).

claims.claim: No admin-centre UI path is documented for the specific classic-Outlook registry control.
claims.quote: Searched: DisableEditPermissions DisableEditDefaultUserPermissions Group Policy user interface Outlook folder permissions. Read restriction article; it documents registry values directly or through Group Policy, but no admin-centre UI path for these values.

claims.claim: The documented registry restriction route is for classic Outlook only.
claims.quote: Restrict users from changing folder permissions in classic Outlook only

claims.claim: With those registry values set, the Permissions tab remains visible and permission-editing options are greyed out.
claims.quote: After you set these registry values, users can still view the Permissions tab in a folder's Properties dialog box. However, the options to modify folder permissions are disabled (grayed out).

claims.claim: The documented Cloud Policy procedure covers classic Outlook, new Outlook and Outlook on the web.
claims.quote: Restrict users from changing folder permissions in classic Outlook, new Outlook, and Outlook on the Web

claims.claim: A Cloud Policy configuration is scoped to a set of users.
claims.quote: Each policy configuration is scoped to a set of users.

claims.claim: The folder-permission restriction article says Cloud Policy changes can take up to 90 minutes to reach Outlook clients.
claims.quote: After a policy configuration is created or changed, it can take up to 90 minutes for the change to be applied to the Outlook clients.
claims.fix: Retain the attributed 90-minute statement, but add that the Cloud Policy overview says desktop Office policies apply when the app is restarted and a user without an assigned configuration can have a 24-hour check-in interval. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy so testing advice does not treat 90 minutes alone as sufficient.
